# Vendored `stripe` stub — committed on purpose

Yes, this is a `node_modules/` directory in git. It is deliberate, and the
root `.gitignore` carries the one-line exception that lets it through
(`!fixtures/**/node_modules/`, right after the global `node_modules/`).

## Why it has to be committed

US-9's guard reads the API version stripe-node pins **implicitly**: since
v12.0.0 the SDK sends a `Stripe-Version` header even when the caller passes no
`apiVersion`, taking it from the generated `apiVersion.js` in its own tarball.
Testing that guard requires an installed `stripe` to read.

The alternatives were worse:

- `npm install stripe@13` in the test suite: network I/O in `npm test`, which
  the tool's own rules forbid (`zero network in the tests`) and which would
  make the suite non-deterministic and slow.
- Mocking the file reads: it would test the mock, not the two real artifacts
  whose shape is the entire risk of US-9.

So the two files the resolver actually reads are vendored, and nothing else.

## What is here, and where it comes from

Both files reproduce what npm ships for `stripe@13.0.0` (tarballs inspected
2026-09-05, 18 versions from 8.222.0 to 22.6.1):

- `package.json` — only the `version` field matters. It answers one boolean
  question, `major >= 12`: *does this SDK pin at all?* It is never used to
  infer a date.
- `cjs/apiVersion.js` — the generated file, in the shape tsc emits for a CJS
  build: the `exports.ApiVersion = void 0;` preamble first, then the real
  assignment `exports.ApiVersion = '2023-08-16';`. That preamble is not
  decoration — it is the trap the reader must survive. Taking "the first
  literal in the file" would yield `'use strict'`, and accepting any
  right-hand side would yield `void 0`.

Nothing else from the package is here. This is not a runnable SDK: no fixture
code under `test/` requires it, and nothing ever will.
